knowledge_gaps.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.
knowledge_gaps.text: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?

mechanisms.description: At atherosclerosis-prone arterial sites, disturbed flow is associated with endothelial stress and senescence, while reduced endothelial nitric-oxide biosynthesis represents the vasomotor dysfunction that impairs dilation. This nonconforming coronary endothelial-function branch is modeled separately from the conserved subendothelial apoB-retention trigger. The cited disturbed-flow evidence derives from mouse carotid arteries and human carotid plaques, so its transfer to coronary endothelial dysfunction is explicitly partial.
mechanisms.name: Endothelial Dysfunction

knowledge_gap.prompt: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: A context is retained as a causal amplifier if MR supports exposure-to-disease directionality and the exposure-attributable risk difference increases across increasing PGS strata; it is flagged as a reverse-causation suspect otherwise.
proposed_experiments.description: Use bidirectional / multivariable Mendelian randomization to test whether each candidate context (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein, smoking) causally affects CAD versus being a consequence of subclinical disease, and whether the causal effect estimate scales with polygenic liability as the amplification model predicts.
proposed_experiments.name: Mendelian randomization of exposure-to-CAD direction across PGS strata

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Amplification is supported if the PGS×context deviation from additivity persists when only pre-diagnosis exposure windows and incident cases are used.
proposed_experiments.description: Restrict exposures to measurements taken well before diagnosis and repeat the PGS×context liability-threshold modelling on incident cases only, to reduce the chance that exposure values reflect behavioural responses to early disease.
proposed_experiments.name: Prospective incident-CAD analysis restricted to pre-diagnosis exposure windows

knowledge_gap.rationale: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

dismech:disorders/Coronary_Artery_Diseas.description: At atherosclerosis-prone arterial sites, disturbed flow is associated with endothelial stress and senescence, while reduced endothelial nitric-oxide biosynthesis represents the vasomotor dysfunction that impairs dilation. This nonconforming coronary endothelial-function branch is modeled separately from the conserved subendothelial apoB-retention trigger. The cited disturbed-flow evidence derives from mouse carotid arteries and human carotid plaques, so its transfer to coronary endothelial dysfunction is explicitly partial.

downstream.description: Connects the vasomotor and disturbed-flow endothelial branch to the conserved retention trigger without asserting that reduced nitric oxide alone is sufficient for apoB retention.

evidence.explanation: Links arterial injury and endothelial dysfunction to subendothelial apoB modification and monocyte entry, but does not isolate nitric-oxide loss or directly establish every intermediate in lipoprotein retention.
evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Arterial injury causes endothelial dysfunction promoting modification of apoB containing lipoproteins and infiltration of monocytes into the subendothelial space.

intermediate_mechanisms: increased endothelial permeability and apoB-lipoprotein entry
downstream.target: Coronary Endothelial Injury and Subendothelial LDL Retention

evidence.explanation: Supports disturbed-flow-associated endothelial senescence as one component of endothelial dysfunction. It does not directly measure nitric-oxide biosynthesis and comes from a mouse carotid model, so it is not treated as direct coronary or nitric-oxide evidence.
evidence.reference_title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of mouse carotid artery under disturbed flow and human carotid plaques identifies key cell populations in atherosclerosis development.
evidence.snippet: CD36 + positive ECs exhibited significant senescence phenotypes following disturbed flow stimulation.

evidence.explanation: Supports disturbed flow as a regional context for atherosclerosis and endothelial dysfunction. It does not directly establish reduced nitric-oxide biosynthesis or a coronary-specific effect.
evidence.reference_title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of mouse carotid artery under disturbed flow and human carotid plaques identifies key cell populations in atherosclerosis development.
evidence.snippet: Atherosclerosis tends to occur in regions of disturbed blood flow. This study explored how disturbed flow aggravates atherosclerosis using single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) datasets from mouse carotid arteries under disturbed flow and human carotid artery plaques.

record.context: Major risk factor for plaque formation

evidence.explanation: EAS consensus statement concludes that LDL is causal for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, supporting elevated LDL cholesterol as a major risk factor for coronary plaque formation.
evidence.reference_title: Low-density lipoproteins cause atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. 1. Evidence from genetic, epidemiologic, and clinical studies. A consensus statement from the European Atherosclerosis Society Consensus Panel.
evidence.snippet: Consistent evidence from numerous and multiple different types of clinical and genetic studies unequivocally establishes that LDL causes ASCVD.

record.name: LDL Cholesterol

readouts.description: Circulating LDL cholesterol indexes the pool of apoB-containing lipoprotein available for retention in the coronary subendothelial space, so its level reports on the intensity of the retention step rather than being caused by it.
readouts.target: Coronary Endothelial Injury and Subendothelial LDL Retention

evidence.explanation: Individual-participant meta-analysis quantifies the association between circulating C-reactive protein and incident coronary heart disease, supporting CRP as an inflammatory risk marker in coronary artery disease.
evidence.reference_title: C-reactive protein concentration and risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and mortality: an individual participant meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Risk ratios (RRs) for coronary heart disease per 1-SD higher log(e) CRP concentration (three-fold higher) were 1.63 (95% CI 1.51-1.76) when initially adjusted for age and sex only, and 1.37 (1.27-1.48) when adjusted further for conventional risk factors

readouts.description: C-reactive protein is a systemic acute-phase index that rises with the inflammatory activity of which intimal monocyte recruitment and foam-cell formation are part. It is a correlate of that intimal process and of coronary risk, not a direct measurement of the lesion.
readouts.target: Monocyte Recruitment and Macrophage Foam Cell Formation

evidence.explanation: INTERHEART, a standardised case-control study of acute myocardial infarction across 52 countries with 15152 cases and 14820 controls. Establishes smoking as one of the largest modifiable contributors to population attributable risk.
evidence.reference_title: Effect of potentially modifiable risk factors associated with myocardial infarction in 52 countries (the INTERHEART study): case-control study.
evidence.snippet: Smoking (odds ratio 2.87 for current vs never, PAR 35.7% for current and former vs never)

evidence.explanation: The tobacco-specific INTERHEART analysis. Quoted for the dose-response relationship, which is the part of the note the odds ratio alone does not establish.
evidence.reference_title: Tobacco use and risk of myocardial infarction in 52 countries in the INTERHEART study: a case-control study.
evidence.snippet: risk increased by 5.6% for every additional cigarette smoked

influences_mechanisms.description: Tobacco smoking raises the risk of acute myocardial infarction in a dose-dependent way. The link is drawn to the clinical event because that is what the cited epidemiology measures; the mediating coronary mechanism is deliberately left unasserted here, as the entry's review notes require.

evidence.explanation: INTERHEART, a standardised case-control study of acute myocardial infarction across 52 countries with 15152 cases and 14820 controls. Establishes smoking as one of the largest modifiable contributors to population attributable risk.
evidence.reference_title: Effect of potentially modifiable risk factors associated with myocardial infarction in 52 countries (the INTERHEART study): case-control study.
evidence.snippet: Smoking (odds ratio 2.87 for current vs never, PAR 35.7% for current and former vs never)

record.name: Smoking
record.notes: Major modifiable risk factor, with a dose-response relationship to myocardial infarction risk.
record.review_notes: The prior note also asserted that smoking promotes endothelial damage. That mechanism is not carried by either epidemiologic source cited here and is not evidenced in this entry; it belongs in pathophysiology with its own citation rather than as an unsourced clause on an exposure.

items.prompt: Which easily-derived clinical variables most reliably predict in-hospital mortality in CAD patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)? Can a simple risk score validated against external cohorts improve prognostic classification beyond conventional risk factors alone, and what patient subtypes remain at highest risk despite optimized antiplatelet and supportive therapy?

Which, if any, pathway beyond change in circulating triglyceride concentration causally mediates the cardiovascular-event contrast observed with high-dose icosapent ethyl: coronary plaque remodeling; altered apolipoprotein-B/remnant burden, composition, trafficking, or retention; platelet effects; inflammatory resolution; endothelial effects; or membrane stabilization and reduced lipid oxidation? How much of the contrast reflects the mineral-oil comparator?
